newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down, gilts steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down, gilts steady in quiet trade.

text.p: Indian call money rates dropped to 4.0 percent for two-day money on Thursday from opening quotes of 5.0-5.5 percent on lower demand, dealers said.
They said call money eased in late morning to around 4.75 percent and fell further to around 4.0 percent by close of trade as demand for funds was poor.

"With the reporting day coming up tomorrow, most banks had finished their borrowing," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There was little trade in overnight money as there is a strike scheduled for tomorrow."
Trade unions have called for a nationwide strike on Friday and bankers said they expected operations to be crippled.
Dealers said prices of government securities were steady in moderate trade.
"Trade will probably pick up on Saturday after the auctions tomorrow," said a dealer. "There were quite a few sellers today."
The Reserve Bank of India holds a repo auction and auctions for 14- and 91-day treasury bills on Friday.
"Once the liquidity positions becomes clear tomorrow, traders will be able to take positions," the dealer said.
Among actively-traded stocks, the 12.59 percent 2004 rose to 100.75 rupees from Wednesday's 100.67.
Other stocks fell with the 13.70 percent 1999 easing to 105.5 from 105.55, the 13.50 percent 1998 to 103.28 from 103.3 and the 13.62 percent 1998 to 104.38 from 104.4 rupees.
